items.title: Berkeley Lab unveils AI-quantum tool for mapping protein structures

featured_image.name: Why 'quantum proteins' could be the next big thing in biology

items.description: Researchers at the Department of Energy's Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and an international team have unveiled a new computing program that combines artificial intelligence with quantum-mechanical calculations to map protein structures faster and more accurately than existing methods. The tool, called AQuaRef — short for AI-enabled Quantum Refinement — was described in a study published in Nature Communications and announced by Berkeley Lab on March 10.[1][2]

items.title: Iran declares U.S., Israeli, allied ships 'legitimate targets' in Hormuz

featured_image.name: The Strait of Hormuz crisis explained: What it means for global shipping

items.description:
Iran's military warned on Wednesday that any vessel belonging to the United States, Israel, or their allies passing through the Strait of Hormuz will be targeted, escalating a maritime crisis that has effectively shut down one of the world's most vital energy corridors.

"Any vessel whose oil cargo or the vessel itself belongs to the United States, the Zionist regime or their hostile allies will be considered legitimate targets," Iran's central operational command, Khatam al-Anbiya, said in a statement carried by state television. The military reiterated that Iran's armed forces "will not allow a single litre of oil to transit" through the strait, adding that the "closure of this strait is the result of conditions imposed by the US and the Zionist regime".[1][2][3]

items.title: IEA proposes record 400M-barrel oil release amid Iran war

featured_image.name: G7 leaders to hold talks to discuss Mideast conflict, oil reserve release

items.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron convened a virtual summit of Group of Seven leaders on Wednesday to address the escalating energy crisis triggered by the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, as oil prices whipsawed and the International Energy Agency proposed the largest release of strategic oil reserves in its history.

The leaders' call came after a week of intensifying economic fallout from the conflict, which began with U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28 and has effectively shut down the Strait of Hormuz — a narrow waterway through which roughly one-fifth of the world's oil supply typically transits. France, which holds the rotating G7 presidency, organized the meeting as governments scrambled to contain the damage to global energy markets.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Markets whipsaw as Iran war escalates and CPI data lands

featured_image.name: European markets head for lower open as Iran war continues

items.description:
Global markets swung between gains and losses on Wednesday as investors navigated an intensifying military conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran alongside fresh consumer inflation data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

The February Consumer Price Index report, released Wednesday morning, covers a period before the U.S.-Iran war broke out on February 28 and was widely expected to show headline inflation holding steady at 2.4% year over year, with a 0.3% monthly increase, according to FactSet estimates cited by Morningstar. Core CPI, which strips out food and energy, was forecast at 0.3% monthly and 2.5% annually. Analysts noted the data would offer limited insight into the economic fallout from the conflict. "This data is from before the recent conflict in the Middle East broke out, so it's not going to give us a whole lot of information on how prices are starting to respond to that," said Josh Jamner, senior investment strategy analyst at ClearBridge, adding that energy price effects would be "a March and April dynamic".[1][2]

items.title: Von der Leyen calls return to Russian energy 'a strategic blunder' amid Iran war

featured_image.name: Speech by President von der Leyen at the European Parliament ...

items.description:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen told the European Parliament on Tuesday that turning back to Russian fossil fuels to ease the energy shock from the Iran war would be "a strategic blunder," even as she acknowledged the conflict has already cost European taxpayers €3 billion in extra energy import costs in just 10 days.[1][2]

Speaking in Strasbourg ahead of the European Council summit scheduled for March 19-20, von der Leyen laid out the scale of the damage: gas prices have risen 50% and oil prices 27% since the U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran began on February 28. "This is the price of our dependency," she said, while insisting that the EU's diversification efforts since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine have left Europe better prepared than before.[3][4][2][1]

items.title: Iran's president's son says new leader is 'safe and sound' amid injury reports

featured_image.name: Slain Ayatollah's son & frontrunner for Supreme Leader is ‘injured in assassination attempt' during air strike

items.description:
Iran's newly appointed Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has not appeared publicly, issued a video address, or released a written statement since the Assembly of Experts declared him the country's third supreme leader on March 9, raising mounting questions about his condition amid an ongoing war with the United States and Israel.

Three Iranian officials told The New York Times that Khamenei, 56, sustained injuries including to his legs during the opening day of the U.S.-Israeli military operation on February 28 — the same strikes that killed his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, along with dozens of other senior officials and members of the Khamenei family. The officials said the new leader "was alert and sheltering at a highly secure location with limited communication".[1][2][3]

items.title: IEA confirms largest-ever oil reserve release at 400M barrels

featured_image.name: IEA countries to meet later Tuesday on release of oil reserves, but ...

items.description:
The International Energy Agency on Wednesday confirmed it will release 400 million barrels of oil from emergency stockpiles, the largest coordinated intervention in the agency's 52-year history, as governments scramble to contain an energy crisis triggered by the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran.

"The oil market challenges we are facing are unprecedented in scale," IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol said in a statement. "IEA member countries have responded with an emergency collective action of unprecedented size."[1]

The decision, announced at 1300 GMT, came ahead of a virtual meeting of Group of Seven leaders chaired by French President Emmanuel Macron to finalize details of the coordinated response. The release more than doubles the previous record of 182 million barrels that IEA member nations distributed in 2022 following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.[2][3][4][5]

items.title: G7 backs IEA's largest-ever oil reserve release amid Iran war

featured_image.name: IEA Will Deploy Emergency Oil Stockpiles

items.description:
The International Energy Agency has proposed releasing up to 400 million barrels from emergency oil stockpiles — the largest coordinated drawdown in the agency's 52-year history — as crude prices remain volatile amid the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz during the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, according to a report first published by The Wall Street Journal on Tuesday.[1]

The proposal, circulated during an emergency meeting of energy officials from the IEA's 32 member nations on Tuesday, March 10, would more than double the previous record of 182 million barrels released in two rounds in 2022 following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. A decision is expected on Wednesday, with the plan set to be adopted unless any member country raises an objection.[2][1]
